cutoverUnits.description: Request timing, protected context, headers, rules, classification, deduplication, and resource-state handoff.
Document-start Worker, fetch, XHR, JSON, TextDecoder, key, manifest, and page-action runtime bundle.
MediaSource capture, bounded page buffering, main spool, reset, finalize, and merge lifecycle.
HLS parse, plan, key, map, range, rendition, live, retry, preprocessing, and byte-output semantics.
DASH parse, plan, BaseURL, timeline, track, range, download, merge, and rejection semantics.
Concurrent transfer, Range, retry, abort, ordered output, cancellation, memory budget, and task ownership.
Verified staged output, leases, ffmpeg, local save, library delivery, normal downloads, external tools, and workflow projection.

capabilities.notes: ElectronNetworkCaptureAdapter is the verified production owner registered once by EmbeddedBrowserCaptureRuntime. It preserves Cat Catch request-stage regex handling and response-start classification, binds redirect hops to fresh onSendHeaders events, cleans pending state on redirect/completion/error/dispose, rejects stale navigation owners, and converts vault invalidation into revisioned Store changes. The legacy onCompleted bridge was removed during network-capture cutover.

acceptedDifferences: When Cat Catch regex classification rewrites a request URL, OmniFlow does not inherit credentials from the observed URL; a new main-owned context is required for the rewritten exact URL.

After an HTTP redirect, OmniFlow never forwards the previous hop's protected headers, including for a same-origin target. The target needs its own main-owned captured context; page-drag staging may still use the captured tab's Electron session cookie jar for cookies scoped to the target URL.
capabilities.notes: The verified main-only vault preserves Cat Catch's protected-header selection and adds bounded pending/retained lifecycles, opaque renderer-safe projection, purpose and owner bindings, independent source/replay resource types, exact resource URL redemption, page-drag Cookie policy, and value-free invalidation events. Production download, inspection, captured-source page drag, external tools, HLS and captured DASH transport redeem fixed-purpose opaque authority; stale and cross-tab owners fail before fetch. Redirects are manual and protected headers never cross hops. Unrecognized/data/blob page-drag and derived uncaptured HLS/DASH URLs remain explicit platform fallbacks without exposing captured header values to renderer. The legacy request-context Map and renderer header DTO were removed during cutover.

The verified pure port covers full-string case-insensitive wildcard page rules, disabled-rule skipping, the default-off Douyin forced block, blacklist/whitelist inversion, and special-page protocol checks. ElectronNetworkCaptureAdapter applies page URL policy to the main-owned current document before recording request context. OmniFlow persisted domain settings intentionally remain a separate product filter over resource/page host and compile through the integration policy.

capabilities.notes: The verified pure port owns ordered request regex, upstream default states, extension/MIME/Content-Disposition/media precedence, hard-break size semantics, wildcard MIME priority and exact-URL dedupe/reset decisions. The OmniFlow policy adds image, key, document and expanded-subtitle kinds without overriding a Cat Catch regex blacklist or non-product rejection. The target settings store preserves the existing schema-2 JSON path, normalization, product defaults and upgrade behavior; production hot-updates compiled settings without replacing the single webRequest listener. Legacy classifier/rules modules were removed during cutover.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow expires captured resource metadata after six hours and releases main-only request contexts on capacity reset, TTL sweep, navigation clear, tab/WebContents disposal, and application disposal; Cat Catch has no equivalent resource TTL or main-only context lifecycle.

OmniFlow stable probe resources upsert by navigation generation plus page-owned resource key. Updating an existing key keeps its opaque id even at capacity, while the same key in a later document creates a new resource instead of merging metadata across pages.

Renderer-safe state exposes opaque resource ids, revision/incarnation stamps, and whitelisted metadata/header capabilities only; page resource keys, context refs and values, page origin, WebContents id, and captured navigation owner facts remain main-owned.
capabilities.notes: The verified main-only ResourceStateStore preserves the desktop 10,000-entry overflow reset/drop behavior, exact-URL dedupe including the 500-fingerprint reset boundary, explicit navigation clear/retain, stable probe upsert, bounded TTL, newest-first snapshots, single-owner context release and revision/incarnation tombstones. Production PageProbeCaptureAdapter binds one document generation to deep-only stable-key writes and keeps resourceKey main-only. Opaque probe resource resolution rechecks tab, incarnation, navigation, origin and WebContents ownership. Vault invalidations feed the same revisioned change path. The legacy tabCaptureStates owner was removed during cutover.

The verified target contracts uniquely own renderer-safe resource/snapshot/change DTOs, whitelist parsing, revision/incarnation reduction and persisted capture-setting DTOs. Main, preload and renderer use those contracts directly or through type-only re-exports. Renderer projections contain opaque IDs, metadata and header capabilities but no page key, context ref, owner identity, URL authority inputs or protected header values. Legacy main DTO copies were removed during cutover.

EmbeddedBrowserCaptureRuntime is the verified production composition and owns exactly one network adapter, context vault, resource store, safe change contract, per-view tokenized probe adapter, opaque access authority and bounded inspection. It owns tab/view registration and replacement, clear/retain navigation, crash quarantine/recovery, spontaneous destruction, explicit close, closeAll, maintenance and app disposal. Probe ingress exists only in deep mode; current and pre-signed next-document tokens are generation-bound and every payload rechecks its owner. Malformed, stale, crashed, disposed and stopped payloads are ignored, MSE control remains on its separate callback, and ordinary discovery keys are main-derived and opaque. The legacy recorder/state path was removed during network-capture cutover.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch begins wrapping real Workers while its Blob Worker probe can still fail asynchronously. The target runtime keeps real Workers native during that short probing state, enables bootstrap injection only after the probe message succeeds, and permanently falls back after error/timeout so CSP cannot strand a page Worker on a rejected Blob URL.

Cat Catch leaves probe and injected Worker Blob URLs live for the document. The target runtime tracks them, revokes the capability probe immediately, bounds injected URLs with a TTL, and exposes idempotent disposal while never terminating page-owned Workers.

Cat Catch only schedules the inline-script scan from DOMContentLoaded. Electron also installs the probe into an already loaded current frame when deep mode starts, so the target adapter schedules the same scan on the next task when readyState is no longer loading; future document-start installs retain the DOMContentLoaded path.
capabilities.notes: The self-contained target installer ports idempotent JSON.parse, TextDecoder manifest, XHR response, fetch clone/body, Worker bootstrap/relay and the Cat Catch slice/subarray/btoa/atob/fromCharCode/DataView/typed-array/join/escape/indexOf experience surfaces. The production document factory now composes that installer with stateful discovery, page helpers, generated-resource ownership and the tokenized main relay. MSE installs first as its separate owner; there is no disabled Deep flag, legacy hook body, whole-probe Worker bootstrap or second relay. The generic composition template and opaque resource action/extract script generators remain platform adapters with executable contracts.

acceptedDifferences: The pure port returns inline manifest bytes instead of creating a page-owned Blob URL. The later page adapter must create the opaque resource from those exact bytes; the executable upstream fixture compares Blob contents rather than nondeterministic Blob URL identities.
capabilities.notes: The fixed search.js findMedia/toUrl path is covered by an upstream-executable fixture. The production discovery session preserves protocol-relative URL handling, the seven-extension allowlist, loose 16-number key coercion, all-zero/ftyp suppression, data-URL manifests, inline MPD, current base expansion and deferred replay when a later hook observation reveals a new base. The page helper preserves playlist gating, base path normalization, raw Vimeo metadata, per-track playlists and the header-only empty master. Generated bytes have one page owner for signature deduplication, Blob/base64, filename, open/export/read and MSE delegation, and production ingress reads the normalized bytes back through the main-owned resource key. Legacy manifest heuristics and probeResources were deleted at cutover.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch relays page-world window.postMessage through a content script and extension background worker. OmniFlow has no extension world, so Electron main issues an unpredictable document token, installs the script through CDP at document start, and accepts console transport only while token, tab, WebContents, incarnation, navigation generation, page origin and deep-mode ownership remain current.
capabilities.notes: ElectronPageProbeEventAdapter rejects tokenless, wrong-token, malformed, stale, stopped, crashed and disposed payloads; PageProbeCaptureAdapter derives owner/resource facts in main. The view installer registers the pre-signed production document script through Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and injects it into mainFrame plus framesInSubtree, tolerating transient frame detachment. Generated manifest/media resources now use this exact ingress and the main ResourceStateStore in production.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch keeps the manual filename and extra-header trimming choices in the injected panel lifetime. OmniFlow's integrated external UI persists all eight product preferences under OmniflowCatchToolkit:* keys in the visited page's origin localStorage; capture enablement remains outside this preference owner and resets with the page runtime.
capabilities.notes: The production page-origin owner fixes checked/empty-string storage semantics, selector/regex validation, reload hydration, fresh-origin reset and blocked-storage fallback. The existing toolkit get/update bridge routes through this owner, which synchronizes a read-only preference projection for the separate MSE actions; immediate manual filename state preserves user whitespace while the derived filename and storage are trimmed. The three page script generators remain platform adapters with an executable forwarding/missing-handler contract. Legacy toolkit storage/state was deleted at cutover.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow emits an authorized trimBeforeHeader marker so the main-owned spool can discard earlier flushed bytes before appending a later initialization header without reading the entire large file back into page memory; Cat Catch performs this decision over its in-memory catchMedia list.
capabilities.notes: The production page adapter now installs the fixed target MSE runtime and keeps DOM actions, filename/Blob handling, and the page-origin toolkit projection at the platform boundary. Pure runtime tests cover append/endOfStream, the optional capture gate, per-track flush/reset, retention limits, completion clearing with and without streams, first-range auto-buffer seeking, cross-flush header replacement, drain header replacement, and drain semantics; production probe characterization covers installation, read/open/export/drain and resource events. Auto-seek intentionally uses the first buffered range, matching fixed Cat Catch behavior for sparse media ranges. When enabled, the page emits a serialized periodic-save control after a flush crosses each configured 1 GiB boundary; main handles it through the same merged/per-track output path and clears the page/spool cache after success. Native playback exceptions continue to propagate once; OmniFlow does not copy Cat Catch's catch-block retry that can invoke a failed native method a second time. Fixed-upstream parity, production-equivalent large-media/auto-download behavior and real-site smoke remain open, so this capability stays porting.

MseSpoolStore is the main-owned spool authority. It serializes per-track writes, reserves bytes before asynchronous append, enforces per-chunk/per-track/global budgets, reaps TTL entries, sweeps stale temp directories at session setup, and clears on reset, navigation, render-process loss, tab close, and controller dispose. Relay authorization binds flush/reset/periodic-save payloads to the current tab's opaque MSE resource key, and the controller serializes those controls per tab so a periodic save observes completed flush writes. Automatic output stages merged or per-track files through the existing browser download completion/import contract and clears page/spool cache only after periodic output succeeds. Merge output now requires a non-empty file after zero-exit ffmpeg and removes partial output on merge failure. A conditional real-binary fixture verifies independent fragmented MP4 video/audio tracks merge into a probeable H.264/AAC MP4; production large-media, full extraction/import and real-site smoke remain open.

acceptedDifferences: Pinned hls.js records the first variable parsing error on the playlist and its evented loader rejects that parse; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same first error because it has no loader event boundary.

Pinned hls.js emits levelEmptyError after manifest loading when a media playlist has no complete fragment; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same No Segments found in Playlist error before creating a download plan.
Pinned hls.js reports malformed media playlists through levelParsingError before LEVEL_LOADED; the synchronous OmniFlow facade throws the same parsing reason before creating a download plan.

Pinned hls.js may reject an all-unknown-codec master later against browser MediaSource support; the OmniFlow pure parser preserves those normal variants for its ffmpeg execution boundary and does not make renderer codec support an execution authority.

Pinned hls.js writes identity explicitly on effective decryptdata; the OmniFlow DTO represents the same identity by omitting optional keyFormat so rewritten local playlists do not gain a redundant KEYFORMAT attribute.

Pinned hls.js exposes null fragment placeholders from a positive EXT-X-SKIP to Cat Catch's external LEVEL_LOADED listener before its internal delta merge, and Cat Catch parseTs then dereferences fragment.url. The synchronous OmniFlow facade reports a stable delta-playlist rejection instead of reproducing that TypeError or silently producing wrong sequence numbers.

Pinned hls.js exposes an empty byteRange array for an init segment without an effective range; the OmniFlow DTO omits its optional byteRange field. Cat Catch checks for exactly two entries and OmniFlow checks field presence, so both issue the same un-ranged init request.

Pinned hls.js marks a fragment encrypted while leaving decryptdata null when a supported EXT-X-KEY has a missing or empty URI; a whitespace-only URI resolves to the playlist URL and Cat Catch attempts to fetch the manifest as key bytes. OmniFlow preserves the encrypted/keyless projection in its plan, then rejects execution before any fetch unless a validated manual AES-128 key can recover the media fragment.

Pinned hls.js preserves zero-length, negative-length, negative-offset, and NaN byte ranges, after which Cat Catch constructs invalid or empty Range headers. OmniFlow preserves hls.js parseInt integer-prefix normalization for valid values but rejects those non-executable ranges before plan creation instead of falling back to an un-ranged full-resource fetch.

Pinned hls.js accepts EXT-X-MAP with a missing, empty, or whitespace-only URI. Missing/empty values replace the current init segment with url="", while whitespace resolves to the playlist URL; Cat Catch then fetches unrelated page or manifest content as init bytes. OmniFlow rejects the manifest before plan creation so it neither retains a stale previous MAP nor fetches an unrelated resource.

Pinned hls.js preserves a middle fragment whose EXT-X-DEFINE substitution yields relurl/url="", advances its duration and sequence, and Cat Catch projects that empty URL to the downloader. OmniFlow rejects the manifest before plan creation instead of fetching an empty target or silently dropping the fragment and shifting later sequence, implicit IV, key, and MAP context.

Pinned hls.js url-toolkit can expose raw fragment URLs containing literal spaces, encoded dot segments, backslashes, or parent traversal above the origin root; Cat Catch then passes those strings to browser fetch, which canonicalizes them to the effective network URL. OmniFlow stores that WHATWG-canonical effective URL directly so exact current-tab resource lookup can retain captured Cookie/Authorization context. The network target is equivalent while the intermediate raw string intentionally differs.

Pinned hls.js MANIFEST_LOADED preserves distinct variant URIs and assigns synthetic pathways when PATHWAY-ID is absent, but Cat Catch builds its choices from MANIFEST_PARSED: content steering exposes only the default implicit pathway, while explicit same-PATHWAY-ID entries collapse to the first URI and attach later groups to it. OmniFlow preserves each unique identity and resolved URI as independently selectable, merges repeated same-URI groups across intervening declarations, and intentionally adds no fallback order or failover semantics.
capabilities.notes: The shared HLS contract, pure Cat Catch parser and pure download-plan projection are the verified DTO/parser/plan owners. Main, preload, renderer and tests import them directly; the old renderer compatibility model was removed during hls-engine cutover. Fixtures lock the pinned hls.js/Cat Catch download boundary for master/media mode isolation, variant/rendition selection, variable substitution, tokenizer/tag dispatch, sequence/discontinuity/duration state, byte ranges, MAP/key context, supported encryption formats, effective IVs, LL-HLS completed-fragment projection, malformed/non-executable rejection and effective URL authority. Deliberate safety differences reject invalid ranges, empty MAP/segment targets, keyless encrypted execution and positive delta placeholders before network work; the acceptedDifferences list records each reason. Cross-URI variants remain independently selectable instead of reproducing Cat Catch MANIFEST_PARSED data loss. Cat Catch tsAddArg remains a fragment-only post-parse transform shared by static, track and live paths. Parent variables and child authority are recovered only from main-owned captured manifests. The bundled jQuery provenance mismatch remains a third-party documentation issue outside this verified HLS runtime behavior.

acceptedDifferences: Cat Catch decrypts AES-128 fragments in its JavaScript downloader; OmniFlow preserves the pure key/IV behavior port but delegates production local-playlist decryption and remuxing to the single cancellable ffmpeg owner, avoiding a second decrypt pass.

Cat Catch's custom key path force-marks every fragment encrypted. OmniFlow applies the same manual AES-128 recovery to media with an encryption signal, or to every media fragment only when the manifest has no key signal at all; it leaves otherwise clear media beside an encrypted MAP clear so a MAP-only key override cannot corrupt mixed playlists.

Pinned hls.js supports full-segment AES-256 CBC/CTR, but Cat Catch's custom m3u8 downloader only instantiates its AES-128-oriented JavaScript decryptor and ffmpeg's HLS demuxer does not recognize the AES-256 METHOD values. OmniFlow restores the vendored hls.js behavior with Web Crypto in the local work-directory pipeline, validates 32-byte keys and 16-byte IVs, decrypts encrypted MAP/media resources, and removes only those locally consumed key tags before ffmpeg.

Cat Catch's custom MAP fetch requests the parser-projected byte range directly and does not reproduce the vendored hls.js FragmentLoader handling for a CBC-encrypted ranged init segment. OmniFlow follows the fixed dependency: it rounds the request to the encrypted block length, fetches the preceding cipher block for a nonzero offset, resets the IV from that block, and writes a clear MAP before ffmpeg. Offsets between 1 and 15 are rejected because no valid previous block can be requested.

Cat Catch delays automatic fragment retries by 500ms times the retry count; OmniFlow immediately requeues the bounded retry, while preserving the same fragment URL and byte Range and allowing the active retry plus pending queue to be cancelled atomically.
capabilities.notes: HlsTaskExecutor is the verified production owner for local key/MAP/media download, rewritten playlists, ffmpeg handoff and failed-fragment retry. The main handler is now a thin target-named adapter for authority, output path, session, IPC and product logging; the old root downloader re-export was removed during hls-engine cutover. Captured URLs redeem through current-tab authority with bounded Range support, while derived uncaptured key/MAP/media URLs use the retained embedded-session adapter. Direct and independent-track paths bind exact opaque authorities and separate protected headers; fragment-query track mode revalidates both children through the captured master and uses isolated workdirs. Retry preserves URL/Range and shares one abort boundary with processors and pending work. AES-128 stays in the local playlist for the cancellable ffmpeg owner; AES-256 and ranged CBC MAP exceptions are pre-decrypted with the pinned hls.js mode/range/IV behavior. Key/MAP resources are deduplicated without collapsing playlist key state. Fake handoff and real ffmpeg/ffprobe tests cover clear, AES-128, AES-256 CBC/CTR and encrypted fMP4 plus independent audio output. The tab/request session owner bounds projections and owns navigation, tab/view loss, controller disposal and shutdown cleanup. Third-party provenance gaps remain tracked by the broader transfer/output capabilities and do not keep a second HLS runtime alive.

HlsLiveTask is the verified production live polling/cumulative-plan owner. It validates selected children through main-owned source authority before their first request, restores only explicitly imported master variables, uses one AbortController across parent/manifest/segment work, accumulates only newly completed EXTINF fragments, and routes navigation, tab/view loss, controller disposal and app exit through the HLS host lifecycle. Feature-scoped library delivery still means tool unmount discards the live task and its frozen output instead of advertising false recovery. The old root recorder re-export was removed during hls-engine cutover. StreamSaver provenance remains tracked under transfer.streaming-memory-budget and does not remain in the HLS runtime.

The verified pure port preserves Cat Catch's conservative PNG/JPEG prefix removal with an unchanged-buffer fallback for incomplete signatures. Local-plan and live paths apply it after rawBuffer emission and before sequential output; captured HLS inspection and the initial live manifest request make exactly one same-URL force-cache attempt after an HTTP failure while retaining main-owned authority headers. Response-less errors, MPD and later live polls do not enter that branch. Fake and real-binary output integrations cover downstream handoff; website-level manual regression remains an environment gap, not a legacy-runtime fallback.

acceptedDifferences: OmniFlow only concatenates static Periods when every Period has the same content type/id/language/primary BaseURL identity and a reusable initialization URL/range; incomplete identities, SegmentBase tracks and init conflicts remain explicit unsupported plans instead of silently switching initialization at a discontinuity.
capabilities.notes: The pure target parser now covers inherited BaseURL alternatives and Period/AdaptationSet/Representation SegmentTemplate, SegmentList and SegmentBase values, static SegmentBase SIDX metadata, SegmentList timeline expansion, static final-segment duration correction, SegmentTemplate endNumber bounds, finite and availability-bounded dynamic SegmentTimeline r=-1, dynamic duration-only SegmentTemplate windows with client clock offset, validated SegmentList ranges, implicit static Period durations derived from the next explicit start or MPD total duration, same-identity static multi-Period concatenation, single-file SegmentBase and DRM evidence through a platform-neutral XML AST. The main-side dash-live-adapter now bounds MPD reads, rejects DTD/entity declarations, parses real XML into that AST and maps the result to the task plan. Incomplete or incompatible multi-Period sets, invalid or structurally ambiguous SegmentList inputs and malformed SIDX responses are explicit rejects; dynamic task execution, init-range splitting and unbounded dynamic repeats without availability evidence remain open; the bundled mpd-parser/jQuery vendor-version discrepancy and complex cross-level array semantics are still open.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/dash-output.test.ts#keeps single-track output on the same cancellable runner
capabilities.notes: DashTaskExecutor now owns bounded plan preflight, range-aware parallel fragment transfer, SIDX index-range fetch and expansion, ordered file writes, external cancellation and temp cleanup. A dynamic plan with a finite current segment window is accepted as a snapshot and uses the same transfer/merge path; empty dynamic windows remain an explicit reject. DashLiveTask now owns injected-snapshot polling, minimumUpdatePeriod clamping, per-representation segment-key dedupe, new-segment delta delivery and abort/stop lifecycle. The main-side dash-live-adapter supplies bounded, DTD/entity-free XML snapshots through an injected fetch and maps the result to DashTaskPlan; appendDashRepresentationSegments writes only new init/media bytes to main-owned track files. EmbeddedBrowserDashLiveSessionOwner keeps live sessions, revisioned task snapshots and tab/view/app cleanup; start/stop/discard are exposed through a separate main/preload IPC contract without renderer UI. The production MPD plan dispatch converts the renderer DTO into the main-side plan, redeems captured-resource authority for fragments and routes local single- or dual-track output through the shared cancellable ffmpeg runner. Generated static and dynamic-refresh fMP4 tracks now have real FFmpeg/FFprobe evidence; SegmentBase supports nested SIDX fetches up to a fixed depth and rejects deeper chains explicitly.

testRefs: electron/service/embeddedBrowserFragmentDownloader.test.ts#stops active requests when its external AbortSignal is cancelled
capabilities.notes: `EmbeddedBrowserFragmentDownloader` now accepts one external AbortSignal and owns the listener for all concurrent fragment requests; HLS and DASH adapters no longer duplicate signal listeners. Retry keeps each fragment's URL/range, and cancellation clears queued work before the single aborted terminal. Ordered output/range terminal race and a uniform task registry entry remain open. Vendor provenance blockers: the bundled jQuery banner reports 4.0.0 while lib/third-party-libraries.md declares 3.7.1; the loaded StreamSaver bundle has the unresolved provenance recorded by transfer.streaming-memory-budget.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/native-download-session.test.ts#cancels the item, cleans staging, and emits a single cancelled terminal event
electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/native-download-session.test.ts#converts a save-path failure into a failed terminal event and releases the session
capabilities.notes: OmniFlow now has a thin `NativeDownloadSession` owner for Electron `will-download`: it assigns a staging path, emits progress/terminal events, cancels by registry, and removes failed or cancelled staging. This is a platform lifecycle port only; Cat Catch's eligible native-download failure fallback into a downloader page, session reuse, and guarded auto-close still require separate integration evidence.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/streaming-transfer.test.ts#rejects oversized streamed content and keeps an existing destination
electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/streaming-transfer.test.ts#cancels an active stream and removes the staged partial file
capabilities.notes: `StreamingTransfer` now writes direct and captured-resource download responses through a bounded Transform into a sibling temporary directory, then publishes only after the complete body succeeds; declared/observed size limits and AbortSignal failures remove only the temporary partial output. The main controller registers these transfers by tab so app or tab cancellation can abort the response. Remaining HTTP IPC consumers, native BrowserWindow downloader fallback, and StreamSaver provenance still require separate migration evidence.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/task-registry.test.ts#rejects new tasks after dispose and remains idempotent
capabilities.notes: `ProcessingTaskRegistry` now owns generic main-side task registration, filtered cancellation, settled-task waiting and idempotent app-exit disposal. The shared ffmpeg executor, legacy external-command adapter, native browser download sessions, and streaming direct/captured-resource transfers register active work here, while protocol-specific HLS/DASH/MSE session owners still retain their domain snapshots and workdir cleanup. Renderer-unmount recovery and broader transfer-task registration remain open.
Current processing reports success with a raw outputPath before local-save or UploadManager delivery reaches a terminal state.

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/staged-output-lease.test.ts#reaps expired staged and claimed files without exposing their paths in snapshots
electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/staged-output-lease.test.ts#requires the claim token to release a claimed output

electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/staged-output-publisher.test.ts#releases the lease and keeps the previous target when processing fails
capabilities.notes: `StagedOutputLeaseStore` now provides a main-only opaque lease base with owner-scoped paths, one delivery claim, TTL touch/reap, and release cleanup; snapshots intentionally omit the real path. `staged-output-publisher.ts#publishStagedOutput` now owns the ordinary direct-file, captured-resource, HLS/MPD direct-manifest, and HLS local-plan download handoffs: processing writes only to the lease path, then a single claim publishes to the user target while preserving the existing final `outputPath` response. HLS live/DASH plan/live/MSE and local-save/UploadManager delivery still return raw paths; crash quarantine, budget accounting, renderer-safe lease IPC, and the application delivery terminal remain open.

HLS now recovers a bounded main-owned task projection after renderer listener remount, but processing and delivery are still not a single application-scoped workflow. In particular, the frozen library target and UploadManager handoff remain feature-scoped, so live recording must discard on tool unmount until this coordinator and staged-output lease exist.
UploadManager is the upload task owner, but the current embedded-browser workflow awaits creation flow rather than maintaining a durable processing/delivery association.
Seed only: filename filtering, template evaluation, large-buffer conversion, and direct data-URL output are anchored, but helper consumers and output semantics remain unmapped.

The current main-process file-save service copies or writes extracted resource bytes to a user-selected path, but delivery terminal state and staged-output release are not yet owned by the planned adapter.

Normal BrowserWindow download completion and optional library import form a separate OmniFlow handoff from captured-output local save and retain their own cleanup lifecycle. Cat Catch browser-download fallback and downloader-page lifecycle are mapped under the transfer capabilities instead of being conflated with this local contract.

testRefs: electron/service/mediaToolFfmpegService.test.ts#returns success only after a non-empty output exists
electron/service/mediaToolFfmpegService.test.ts#returns failure and removes partial output on ffmpeg failure
electron/service/embedded-browser/processing/ffmpeg-executor.test.ts#dispose aborts and waits for active tasks before returning
capabilities.notes: Manifest download and manifest track merge now share a cancel-aware process runner: HLS calls register its AbortSignal with the tab/request owner, termination uses the cross-platform process-tree adapter, and aborted/non-zero tasks remove partial output. Every manifest input receives its own protocol whitelist and allowed-extension policy before its input declaration, so a second encrypted track can resolve its local key instead of inheriting ffmpeg's default extension rejection. Conditional real-binary integrations verify the manifest runner produces a probeable MP4/AAC output from generated local HLS and merges AES-128 encrypted fMP4/H264 video with an independent AES-128/AAC track into one probeable MP4. Resource merge/transcode, DASH local-file merge and the media-tool operations now use the same executor and output contract; executable probing remains a separate short-lived process, and no application-wide task/app-exit registry exists yet.

testRefs: electron/service/embeddedBrowserExternalTools.test.ts#keeps launched commands registered until their process exits
electron/service/embeddedBrowserExternalTools.test.ts#lets app shutdown cancel and await an external command
electron/service/embeddedBrowserExternalTools.test.ts#encodes the complete custom protocol payload as UTF-8 Base64
capabilities.notes: Pinned upstream Base64-encodes m3u8dl custom-protocol payloads when configured. The production ExternalToolDispatcher accepts only tabId, opaque resourceId, and toolKey, redeems URL/metadata/protected headers from the main-owned Store/Vault, and rejects invalid, cross-tab, or stale requests before execution. The protocol adapter now exposes an opt-in `encodePayload` setting that Base64-encodes the complete template payload after its scheme delimiter, preserving the default plain custom-protocol behavior. The legacy executor keeps spawned local commands registered until their real process exit, supports graceful-then-force tree termination during app shutdown, and preserves the fast dispatch return behavior. Broader production wiring coverage and legacy cleanup remain open. Options import/export is a separate peripheral Base64 consumer and remains outside this initial runtime mapping.
